title: Jenkins Fundamentals
description: Learn to set up Jenkins, configure jobs, and use the web UI for pipeline management.

data.text: **Jenkins** is an open-source automation server widely used to orchestrate CI/CD pipelines. Written in Java, it provides a rich web UI for configuring build jobs and a plugin ecosystem with over 1,800 extensions. Jenkins can build, test, and deploy applications written in virtually any language.

terms.definition: A machine (physical or virtual) that is part of the Jenkins cluster and runs jobs.
A repeatable automation task in Jenkins — e.g., a build, test, or deploy job.
An extension that adds integrations and functionality to Jenkins.
The directory on a node where a job's files are checked out and built.

data.text: Jenkins runs on a **master** (now called the controller) that coordinates jobs and stores configuration. **Agents** (formerly called nodes or slaves) execute builds on behalf of the master. In small setups, the master can act as its own agent, but production deployments separate these roles for scalability and security.

data.title: Getting the initial admin password
data.text: When Jenkins starts for the first time, it generates an admin password. Find it with: `docker exec jenkins cat /var/jenkins_home/secrets/initialAdminPassword`

A **job** in Jenkins is a configured task. You can create a *Freestyle project* for simple builds, a *Pipeline* job for code-based pipelines, or a *Multibranch Pipeline* that automatically discovers and runs pipelines for each git branch.

data.text: Go to **Manage Jenkins → Manage Plugins** to browse and install plugins. Alternatively, install plugins at startup using the `--init-path` flag or the `jenkins-plugin-cli` tool inside the Docker image.

data.title: Set up Jenkins locally
data.description: Get a local Jenkins instance running and create your first job.
steps: Start Jenkins with Docker: `docker run -d -p 8080:8080 jenkins/jenkins:lts-jdk17`.
Unlock Jenkins using the initial admin password from the container logs.
Create a freestyle job that clones a small public repo and runs a build step.
Run the job and check the console output.
Add a post-build action to archive artifacts.
data.expectedOutcome: A running Jenkins instance with a configured job that builds successfully.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Jenkins is an open-source automation server for CI/CD with a rich plugin ecosystem.
The master-agent architecture separates coordination from execution.
Jobs can be freestyle, pipeline-based, or multibranch — choose based on complexity.
Plugins extend Jenkins; essential ones include Git, Pipeline, and Docker Pipeline.
data.takeaway: Jenkins is highly extensible — start simple with a freestyle job, then move to pipelines as needs grow.
